policy.positioning: XGuard protects children without becoming a surveillance product

firstWaveStrategy: Contact high-leverage international networks and regulators first, then use their referrals and country networks for national outreach instead of sending indiscriminate mail to every government office.

targets.ask: Validate country child-helpline routing and discuss a technical child-safety referral partnership.

targets.organization: National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC)
targets.ask: Discuss program-partner fit, CyberTipline routing boundaries and safe referral design.

targets.organization: European Commission — DG CONNECT / Better Internet for Kids
targets.ask: Request a technical and safeguarding dialogue on rights-respecting child-safety controls and DSA protection-of-minors alignment.
Request dialogue on technology-facilitated child sexual exploitation and abuse safeguards and potential ecosystem participation.
Validate XGuard's CSAM reporting handoff design and boundaries. Never send suspected CSAM files by email.
Request guidance on appropriate engagement for a child-safety technical control supporting regulated services' protection duties.

countryRollout.method: Add a national government, regulator, police/cybercrime unit, hotline or child-protection authority only after verifying the exact competent contact from an official government or recognized child-safety source.
preferredReferralPath: European Commission / national Digital Services Coordinators where applicable
recognized national child-protection or online-safety regulator
countryRollout.fallback: Use XGuard's verified global reporting directory rather than inventing a national contact.
